name: Trap Botox (Barbie Botox)
lead: Trap Botox, popularly called "Barbie Botox", is the injection of botulinum toxin into the trapezius muscle, aimed at relaxing the muscle so the neck appears longer and the shoulder line slimmer. It is an off-label cosmetic use of a toxin.[1]

A 2024 systematic review in the Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery examined the trend.[1] Trapezius injection has also been used in clinical settings such as chronic migraine and cervical dystonia protocols.[2][3]

paras: The procedure aims to reduce trapezius bulk using a neuromodulator so the neck-shoulder line looks elongated.[1]

The 2024 systematic review is the main published synthesis of the trend.[1] Registered trials of toxin in neck and trapezius muscles concern medical conditions such as cervical dystonia and chronic migraine, not appearance.[2][3]

No studies found of trapezius toxin for cosmetic neck appearance beyond the systematic review cited above;[1] registered trials involving trapezius injection address cervical dystonia and migraine.[2][3]

card.summary: Toxin injected into the trapezius to make the neck look longer; a 2024 systematic review exists, cosmetic data are thin.
card.note: Off-label; neck and shoulder muscle weakness is a general toxin concern.

quick.overview:
Trap Botox means injecting botulinum toxin into the trapezius so the neck looks longer and the shoulder slope softer. It went viral as "Barbie Botox".

A 2024 systematic review covers the trend.
quick.mechanism: The toxin weakens the injected muscle so it relaxes and reduces bulk over time.
quick.risks: It is an off-label use of a prescription product. Detailed outcome data were not reviewed.
